messages.subject: Paired boxplots
parts:
Hi!

I'm using this command to get a set of boxplots for each of 2 groups:
> ggplot(a, aes(x = variable, y = value)) + geom_boxplot()+ scale_y_continuous(trans="log10") + facet_wrap(~ AGE)
(many empty elements because a is just an small subset of the actual
dataset)

But what I would actually want is one panel in which boxes were
paired, left for "OLD", and right for "MOD", so that the 2 groups can
be compared by the distribution in each element.

The only way I can think of is actually splitting each element into 2
(i.e., CaOLD and CaMOD), is there a more elegant way?

Thanks
Agus

messages.subject: Re: Paired boxplots
parts:
How about using colour or fill to have them right next to each other?

For example, 


ggplot(a, aes(x = variable, y = value)) + geom_boxplot(aes(colour=AGE))+  scale_y_continuous(trans="log10")



B
